title: Seven places Bollywood stars keep returning to that aren't Goa or Maldives
excerpt: Beyond Goa and the Maldives, Bollywood's most loyal holiday rituals play out in London, Gstaad, Dubai, New York, Paris, Bali and Kashmir — a star-tested itinerary any traveller can borrow.
body:
• Forget Goa and Maldives: Bollywood's most loyal vacation rituals play out in London, Gstaad, Dubai, New York, Paris, Bali and Kashmir.
  • The patterns are generational — Shah Rukh Khan's annual London runs, the Saif–Kareena December pilgrimage to snow-covered Gstaad, Ranbir Kapoor's second-home relationship with New York.
  • Most of these destinations are directly reachable from US gateways, making the star itinerary unusually practical for diaspora travellers.
  • Each spot offers a distinct draw: ski-season Alpine luxury, monsoon-warm Himalayan valleys, old-world city culture, or tropical wellness.

Goa and the Maldives get the Instagram posts, but Bollywood's longest-running travel habits live elsewhere. When stars get a real break — not a shoot, not a promotional tour — they return to the same handful of places year after year: some for snow, some for shopping, some for the privacy that only a familiar city provides. Here are seven destinations that have earned repeat visits, and what makes each worth borrowing for your own holiday.

London — Shah Rukh Khan, Alia Bhatt

London is the default setting of Bollywood's holiday calendar. Shah Rukh Khan has made the city his annual escape for years — his children studied there, and he once called it his favourite city "in all ways and things that I like." Alia Bhatt has said that whenever she thinks of travelling, she ends up landing in London. The formula is privacy plus texture: Hyde Park mornings, the West End, Notting Hill, serious shopping — and relative freedom from the crowds that gather everywhere else they go.

Gstaad, Switzerland — Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan

This is Bollywood's most ritualised holiday. Saif and Kareena have turned their Gstaad trip into an annual December fixture: snow, Alpine quiet, and a chalet-town that does discretion well. The couple, with their children, visits when a thick blanket of snow turns the place into what one travel account called "a silver heaven." If you go, the December–February window is the point; the town is built for ski-season living.

Dubai — Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan

Dubai is the quick-gateway habit: a few hours from Mumbai, luxury shopping, desert safaris, beach time by day and water sports by night. SRK's relationship with the city runs so deep that Dubai Tourism has featured him in its "Be My Guest" campaigns and lit up the Burj Khalifa for his birthday. Salman Khan treats it as a default long weekend — food, shopping, spas, and the infrastructure to switch from adventure to indulgence in minutes.

New York City — Ranbir Kapoor, Priyanka Chopra Jonas

New York is Ranbir Kapoor's second home — Broadway, Central Park, the Met, SoHo — a city whose energy matches his family's industry-sized ambitions. Priyanka Chopra Jonas splits her actual life between Mumbai and the US, and NYC gets the leisure visits. For diaspora travellers on the East Coast, this is the easiest star itinerary of all: a weekend in a city many already live near.

Paris — Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli

Paris remains the romantic capital of the celebrity itinerary. Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli have repeatedly chosen its streets for quiet getaways — the Seine, Montmartre, the Louvre, and the Michelin-starred end of the dining spectrum. Shah Rukh Khan counts Paris as his second favourite city after London, and Janhvi Kapoor has walked its cobblestones too. Spring and early autumn are the kindest seasons for it.

Bali — Alia Bhatt, Shraddha Kapoor, Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput

Bali is Bollywood's wellness-and-villa escape: jungle resorts in Ubud, beach clubs in Seminyak, temple towns and spa therapies. Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput have vacationed here for the secluded-luxury version of the island, while Alia Bhatt and Shraddha Kapoor lean toward its yoga-and-café calm. The April–October window brings the best weather; Ubud for stillness, Nusa Dua for pure resort luxury.

Kashmir — Sara Ali Khan

The domestic outlier on the list, and the one most Indians can reach fastest. Sara Ali Khan has repeatedly escaped to the valley — Dal Lake's houseboats, the meadows of Gulmarg, the peaks of Sonamarg. Veteran actors Asha Parekh and Waheeda Rehman have long shared the affection. Snow season (December–February) is for Gulmarg's slopes; April–June is for tulips and the valley in full bloom.

Planning the star treatment

What the seven have in common is familiarity, not novelty. The stars return to places they know well enough to be bored in, happily. That is a useful travel principle: the best trip is often the second or third visit, when you stop sightseeing and start living there for a while. From the US, London, New York and Dubai are direct-flight easy; Gstaad, Paris, Bali and Kashmir reward the extra leg. Book the December Alpine trips early — if it is the season the stars are going, it is the season everyone else is too.
